title: Messaging mux — shared definitions for DID multiplexing at a mediator
description: Shared $def objects referenced by the messaging/mux/* specifications: the scope vocabulary, grant states, attach and detach reasons, the grant and attachment views, and the three signed statements — session attach, stored grant, revoke-all — each a closed JSON object carrying an embedded W3C Data Integrity proof by the member DID. Not itself a Trust Task specification (the `_shared` folder is skipped by the registry build).

MuxDid.title: MuxDid
MuxDid.description: A DID, carried verbatim and compared by exact string equality. Unlike the messaging family's `Vid`, never a hash: the mediator resolves it to verify a statement signed by it. For a member DID reached over TSP, the TSP VID is the DID itself.

MuxScopeValue.title: MuxScopeValue
MuxScopeValue.description: One capability a member DID extends to a principal's connection. `receive`: live delivery of the member's inbound messages on the connection. `pickup`: message-pickup status and delivery requests naming the member as `recipient_did`, and inclusion in a raw-TSP inbox drain. `delete`: deleting the member's stored messages, including delete-on-ack and delete-on-send; a member without `delete` keeps its messages in its inbox until something holding `delete` collects them. `send`: the mediator accepts on this connection frames whose sender is the member DID — the frame is still signed or authcrypted with the member's own keys; the scope only lets the mediator accept it on this socket.

MuxScope.title: MuxScope
MuxScope.description: A set of capabilities: a non-empty JSON array of MuxScopeValue, compared as a set — order is not significant and a repeated value collapses into one. Never empty: an empty scope is refused, never read as "all". There is no default scope anywhere — every attach and every grant names its scope explicitly. A scope is always bounded by the member DID's own access-control capabilities at the mediator.

StatementScope.title: StatementScope
StatementScope.description: The scope a member DID signs into a statement: a JSON array of MuxScopeValue, compared as a set — order is not significant and a repeated value collapses. It MUST NOT be empty; an empty signed scope is refused with the task's `emptyScope` code, never read as "all". Unlike MuxScope, emptiness is not a schema failure here, so that the refusal is reported per statement rather than failing the whole batch.

MuxRole.title: MuxRole
MuxRole.description: The side of a delegation a requester acts as. `principal`: the DID that authenticated the connection and to which members' traffic is delegated. `member`: a DID whose traffic is delegated.

MuxSource.title: MuxSource
MuxSource.description: How a member came to be on a connection: through a stored grant, or through a session attach bound to that connection.

GrantId.title: GrantId
GrantId.description: A grant's identifier, chosen by the member DID's signer and carried in its grant statement; a UUID is RECOMMENDED. A mediator refuses a grant whose identifier is already on the member DID's record.

SessionId.title: SessionId
SessionId.description: The mediator's identifier for one authenticated connection, as announced in that connection's `ready` event.

MuxNonce.title: MuxNonce
MuxNonce.description: 32 random bytes, base64url without padding, that belong to exactly one connection and are never reused. Attach statements sign over it, which is what makes an attach statement unusable on any other connection.

GrantState.title: GrantState
GrantState.description: A stored grant's state. `active`: valid; the member is attached whenever the principal is connected. `suspended`: the member DID proved control with a key that signed none of its active grants (the unknown-key rule); terminal — the grant cannot be resumed and must be recreated by a fresh member signature. `staleKey`: the key that signed the grant is no longer in the member DID's current authentication relationship; terminal — it does not become active again if the key reappears. `expired`: an active grant past its effective expiry; computed when read, never stored. `epochRevoked`: the member DID advanced its epoch with messaging/mux/revoke-all. A grant revoked with messaging/mux/revoke has no state: it is deleted. A dead grant (every state but `active`) stays listable for the mediator's retention window after its effective expiry, then is pruned.

AttachReason.title: AttachReason
AttachReason.description: Why a member became attached to a connection. `connect`: a stored grant re-validated when the principal authenticated. `grant`: a grant was stored while the principal was connected. `attach`: a session attach. `reactivated`: a member that was attached but inactive, because the member DID's own direct connection took precedence, became active when that direct connection ended.

DetachReason.title: DetachReason
DetachReason.description: Why a member left a connection, or why a stored grant did not attach on connect. `revokedByMember` / `revokedByPrincipal`: messaging/mux/revoke by that side. `epochBumped`: the member DID ran messaging/mux/revoke-all. `suspendedUnknownKey`: the unknown-key rule suspended the grant. `keyRotated`: the grant's signing key left the member DID's current authentication relationship (grant state `staleKey`). `expired`: the grant or attach reached its effective expiry. `accountBlocked`: the member's account was blocked. `superseded`: the member DID's own direct connection, or a newer connection of the same kind, now receives its live traffic; the member stays on this connection inactive. `admin`: an operator acted. `detachRequested`: the principal removed a session attach with messaging/mux/detach. `accountRemoved`: the member's account, or the principal's, was removed. `resolutionFailed`: the member DID could not be resolved when the grant was re-validated; the grant is not changed and is re-checked later.

MemberChangeReason.title: MemberChangeReason
MemberChangeReason.description: The reason carried by one member's change in a messaging/mux/event `attached` or `detached` event: exactly the AttachReason values followed by the DetachReason values, with their meanings. An `attached` event carries only AttachReason values and a `detached` event only DetachReason values. One closed set rather than a union, so every generated binding types it as one enumeration; it MUST be kept equal to the two sets it joins.

GrantRef.title: GrantRef
GrantRef.description: Identifies one stored grant and the two parties to it.

principal.description: The principal DID the grant delegates to.

GrantView.title: GrantView
GrantView.description: The mediator's view of one stored grant, as messaging/mux/list and messaging/mux/update return it: the grant statement verbatim, with the state and the effective scope and expiry beside it.

statement.description: The grant statement exactly as the member signed it and the mediator stored it, proof included, so either party can re-verify it.

scope.description: The effective scope: the signed scope, or the narrower one messaging/mux/update set.

expiresAt.description: The effective expiry: the signed `exp` rendered as RFC 3339, or the earlier one messaging/mux/update set.

narrowed.description: True when messaging/mux/update narrowed the effective scope or expiry below what the statement signs.

attachedNow.description: Principal view only: whether the member is attached through this grant to the connection that carried the list request.

AttachView.title: AttachView
AttachView.description: One session attach on a connection.

expiresAt.description: When the attach lapses: its signed `exp`.

deliveryActive.description: False while live traffic for the member goes elsewhere — to the member DID's own direct connection, which takes precedence over a mux connection.

MuxDataIntegrityProof.title: MuxDataIntegrityProof
MuxDataIntegrityProof.description: The W3C Data Integrity proof embedded in a mux statement, made by the member DID: the format and verifier Trust Tasks already use for document proofs (SPEC §4.7). The proof covers the whole statement except `proof` itself, as the cryptosuite defines. Closed: a member Data Integrity defines but this list omits is refused.

cryptosuite.description: The W3C Data Integrity EdDSA cryptosuite used.

verificationMethod.description: The DID URL of the verification method that signed. MUST be controlled by the statement's `issuer` and listed in that DID's current `authentication` relationship.

proofPurpose.description: MUST be `authentication`. Any other value is refused with `messaging/mux:proofPurposeInvalid` — a proof made for another relationship (an `assertionMethod` credential signature, say) is never accepted as control of the DID.

created.description: OPTIONAL: when the proof was made, as Data Integrity defines it. Covered by the proof; the statement's own `iat` is what the mediator checks.

AttachStatement.title: AttachStatement
AttachStatement.description: A member DID's statement that the named principal may carry its traffic on one connection — the one whose `sessionId` and `muxNonce` it names — until `exp`, within `scope`. Signed by the member with an embedded Data Integrity proof whose purpose is `authentication`.

type.description: Always `muxAttach`; names the statement kind, so a statement of one kind is never accepted as another.

issuer.description: The member DID: the signer, and the DID the statement concerns.

audience.description: The mediator's DID. A statement names exactly one mediator and is refused by every other.

principal.description: The principal DID the connection is authenticated as. MUST differ from `issuer`.

iat.description: JWT NumericDate (RFC 7519 §2), whole seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z UTC: when the statement was signed. MUST NOT be more than 60 seconds in the mediator's future.

exp.description: JWT NumericDate (RFC 7519 §2): when the statement stops being accepted. REQUIRED; MUST be after `iat` and in the future.

GrantStatement.title: GrantStatement
GrantStatement.description: A member DID's standing statement that the named principal may carry its traffic at this mediator, on any connection, until `exp`, within `scope`, under the member's current `epoch`. Signed by the member with an embedded Data Integrity proof whose purpose is `authentication`, and stored verbatim by the mediator as the only evidence of the delegation.

type.description: Always `muxGrant`; names the statement kind, so a statement of one kind is never accepted as another.

issuer.description: The member DID: the signer, and the DID the statement concerns.

audience.description: The mediator's DID. A statement names exactly one mediator and is refused by every other.

principal.description: The principal DID that may carry the member's traffic. MUST differ from `issuer`.

epoch.description: The member DID's current epoch at the mediator. Only messaging/mux/revoke-all advances it.

iat.description: JWT NumericDate (RFC 7519 §2), whole seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z UTC: when the statement was signed. MUST NOT be more than 60 seconds in the mediator's future.

exp.description: JWT NumericDate (RFC 7519 §2): when the statement stops being accepted. REQUIRED; MUST be after `iat` and in the future.

RevokeAllStatement.title: RevokeAllStatement
RevokeAllStatement.description: A member DID's statement, proving current control of it, that every grant on it signed under `epoch` or earlier is void. Signed by the member with an embedded Data Integrity proof whose purpose is `authentication`.

type.description: Always `muxRevokeAll`; names the statement kind, so a statement of one kind is never accepted as another.

issuer.description: The member DID: the signer, and the DID the statement concerns.

audience.description: The mediator's DID. A statement names exactly one mediator and is refused by every other.

epoch.description: The epoch being voided: the member DID's current one.

iat.description: JWT NumericDate (RFC 7519 §2), whole seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z UTC: when the statement was signed. MUST NOT be more than 60 seconds in the mediator's future.

exp.description: JWT NumericDate (RFC 7519 §2): when the statement stops being accepted. REQUIRED; MUST be after `iat` and in the future.
